# Generated context — the files a session reads are written by code

Every Vodou session starts by reading a small set of workspace files from
`.vodou/workspace/`. Until September 2026 several of those were typed by hand,
and they drifted: a capability list went four months without matching the binary
it described, and a manual pointer named a copy that was never updated after
install.

Now **every file a session reads is regenerated by code from a source of truth**,
on a clock. You never have to maintain them — and you can still correct them.

## The three generated files

| file | rendered by | source of truth | how to change what it says |
|---|---|---|---|
| `MEMORY.md` | `memory_render` | `memory.db` — pins first, then this week, then this project, then global | pin, unpin, or `vodou-core mem edit` |
| `TOOLS.md` | `vodou-core workspace render` | the **running binary's** command tree, plus paths that actually exist | edit `templates/TOOLS.md` for the static tail |
| `HEARTBEAT.md` | `heartbeat::directive` | your Heartbeat pins | edit the pins, not the file |

Each file says so in its first lines:

```
# MEMORY.md — rendered from memory.db
<!-- rendered by vodou-core memory_render at … · this is a SNAPSHOT: edits here are overwritten on the next render — pin a memory instead -->
```

`TOOLS.md` lists commands from the clap tree of **this** binary, so a release that
adds a verb shows it on the next tick with no template for anyone to remember to
edit.

## Correcting a generated file

Editing a rendered file directly is safe, because the edit is **adopted rather
than overwritten**:

```bash
vodou-core mem edit        # opens the rendered MEMORY.md in $EDITOR
```

On close, the **diff** becomes operations against `memory.db`:

- a line you added becomes a pin;
- a line you deleted is marked wrong — the chunk is invalidated, **never deleted**,
  and it stays gone on the next render;
- a line you did not touch produces nothing.

That last rule is what makes it safe: re-saving an unchanged file is a no-op, and
an auto-selected line is never silently adopted as a pin just because it was in
the file when you saved.

The Memory page in the console does the same thing through a preview: nothing is
written until you apply, and a save whose underlying render has moved since you
opened it is refused with the current content, so your edit is preserved rather
than clobbered.

## Files that no longer exist

`USER.md`, `IDENTITY.md` and `SOUL.md` were retired on 2026-09-09, and the workspace
copy of `AGENTS.md` on 2026-09-10. Their content moved to owners that code can
read: names to settings, facts and preferences to pins, boundaries to Boundary
pins. The originals were archived to `backups/retired-<date>/`, not deleted.

```bash
vodou-core workspace retire --dry-run
```

`retire` moves a leftover file to the archive and **refuses** any file that still
has a live reader, naming the reader.

A commit guard (`scripts/workspace-guard.py`) blocks new code that reads or writes
a hand-maintained workspace file, so a retired file cannot quietly acquire a
reader again.

## Is it still running?

`vodou-core flows` grades it (Flow 18): *is every generated context file still
being regenerated?* A renderer that stopped would leave a file that still reads
plausibly — which is exactly the failure a hand-maintained file had.
